speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness in your upper limbs. To determine the cause, have you noticed any slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your handwriting recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of double vision worsening with up/down gaze and fatigable limb weakness that improves with rest is highly characteristic. I will not pursue further tests as the clinical presentation is classic and sufficient for a definitive diagnosis.
